source_review.notes: Checked all ten final NASA references on 2026-08-31; every URL returned HTTP 200. Reviewed Product Validation, verification/validation distinctions, stakeholder expectations, technical planning, V&V and ConOps outlines, Phase E operational validation, current NASA-STD-3001 human-centered processes and human-performance material, and NPR 7123.1B. Intended use, intended environment, MOEs, ConOps, controlled articles, representative users, off-nominal scenarios, human-in-the-loop evidence, and configuration-bound reporting remain source-contextual.

evidence: Reviewed operational context tuple C=(U,G,E,X,D,P,R,L) and every component definition.
Reviewed the bounded evidence relation E_v models V(S_v,C_v,B,M).
Reviewed stakeholder expectation set B, scenario s_k, coverage map K, MOE tuple, and fidelity vector F.
Confirmed the text denies universal proof, certification, future-performance, and transfer claims from the notation.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Symbols are defined locally and represent a structured assurance claim, not a formal decision procedure for operational effectiveness.

evidence: Executed operational-validation-scenario-fixture under python3 with exact output in artifacts/snippets/SYSENG-077/report.json.
Confirmed five scenarios cover all six declared context dimensions while only four initial MOEs pass.
Confirmed 145 seconds exceeds the 120-second handoff limit and correctly yields initial_claim=not_supported.
Confirmed the synthetic 110-second post-remediation observation passes the declared threshold and all five scenario rules.
Recomputed Exercise 2 rates as 98%, 85%, 80%, and 80%, with pooled 127/135=94.074074...%.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The fixture and exercise use observed deterministic/sample arithmetic only; neither estimates a population success probability or causal remediation effect.

evidence: Confirmed verification conformance does not entail intended-use fitness when stakeholder expectations or operational context are incomplete.
Confirmed scenario-cell coverage does not entail adequate depth, representativeness, interaction coverage, or statistical confidence.
Confirmed high fidelity in one dimension cannot compensate for a low-fidelity dimension that controls the outcome without a justified transfer model.
Confirmed a pooled rate cannot compensate for a failing mandatory scenario-class threshold.
Confirmed evidence for one configuration/context does not automatically transfer across changed users, environments, external systems, data, procedures, support, or lifecycle modes.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The reasoning relies on bounded implication limits and counterexamples rather than a universal theorem of validation completeness.

evidence: Challenged nominal, peak, boundary, degraded, contingency, emergency, recovery, maintenance, transition, rollback, and retirement conditions.
Challenged expert/developer participant bias, training contamination, language, accessibility, fatigue, shift, team authority, and affected stakeholder omission.
Challenged laboratory/field differences, visual versus dynamic fidelity, perfect external services, clean synthetic data, time compression, and unlimited support.
Challenged aggregate averages, small samples, rare critical classes, missing observations, subgroup failure, learning/order effects, and false probability claims.
Challenged unsafe realism, privacy/security constraints, workarounds, procedure-only correction, anomaly blame, production telemetry overcredit, and post-release context drift.
Reviewed all ten examples and five complete answers for assumptions, intermediate reasoning, evidence limitations, and bounded conclusions.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Real validation requires relevant stakeholder, operator, domain, human-factors, operations, safety, security, statistics, test, support, configuration, and acceptance expertise as applicable.

evidence: Confirmed claims trace to baselined stakeholder expectations, ConOps, intended use, MOEs, authority, and exclusions.
Confirmed the evaluated system includes required people, procedures, data, facilities, external services, training, maintenance, support, and governance.
Confirmed every result remains bound to article/configuration, participants, context, scenarios, tools, procedures, and evidence.
Confirmed applicable adversity, representative participation, proxy-fidelity limits, and disaggregated critical outcomes cannot be replaced by nominal aggregate success.
Confirmed anomalies remain visible through correction/disposition, regression, residual risk, and claim-scope update.
Confirmed operational/context/configuration changes trigger validation impact analysis.
invariant_checking.notes: A requirement pass, customer demonstration, realistic appearance, expert success, average pass, production deployment, or historical validation is never treated as sufficient by itself.

proof_review.notes: The chapter contains no formal proof or theorem requiring proof review; it presents bounded evidence relations, arithmetic, and counterexamples.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No passage is labeled or presented as a proof sketch.

evidence: Executable output is labeled synthetic_single_observation_scenarios_only.
Fixture limitations deny completeness, representativeness, causality, durability, measurement, sampling, safety, and real operational claims.
Worked examples and pilot arithmetic are teaching cases, not field studies, acceptance decisions, certifications, or population estimates.
Official NASA sources are attributed without claiming NASA review or endorsement of the chapter.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Synthetic execution, source-backed guidance, internal review, controlled operational evidence, acceptance, and certification remain distinct.

conceptual_review.notes: Internal conceptual review checked verification, requirements validation, qualification, system validation, acceptance and certification distinctions; intended use; operational context; stakeholder expectations; ConOps; MOEs; scenarios; representativeness; fidelity; total-system outcomes; anomalies; bounded claims; and lifecycle revalidation.

practitioner_review.notes: Internal practitioner-oriented review checked claim definition, stakeholder authority, scenario portfolios, participant/data/environment selection, simulator and article pedigree, safe execution, mission-thread observations, disaggregated analysis, anomaly correction, operational restrictions, readiness, monitoring, and revalidation triggers.

pedagogical_review.notes: Internal pedagogical review confirmed progression from claim and context modeling through scenario design, fidelity, execution, analysis, and decision. Ten distinct examples and five complete solutions cover field response, remote monitoring, clinical coordination, data semantics, maintenance, continuity, simulators, user sampling, rare critical cases, and context change.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external NASA expert, stakeholder, operator, affected-community representative, domain engineer, human-factors specialist, statistician, safety/security reviewer, test organization, operations/support owner, configuration authority, independent V&V organization, acceptance authority, certification body, or other external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
